reason: The intro says muscle precursors join, and the pictured fusion proteins sit where adjacent precursors meet.
expectation: The precursor cells should join into a longer cell with multiple nuclei.

effect: The precursors fused into one muscle fibre with many nuclei and sliding filaments. Its grip sites are still covered, so I will try the calcium signal next.
reaction: It is interesting that one muscle fibre is a single cell with many nuclei.
reason: The goal is to make the fibre pull, and the calcium pulse is pictured spreading around its filaments.
expectation: The calcium signal should allow the filaments to interact and the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium uncovered the grip sites, letting the filaments slide and the fibre shorten. The fibre still needs to become ready again.
reaction: It is surprising that the fibre shortens without the filaments themselves shortening.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes have pumps and ATP, suggesting they can return calcium to storage so the fibre can reset.
expectation: Calcium should be pumped back into storage, allowing the fibre to relax and become ready again.

effect: Calcium was pumped back into storage, stopping the pull and leaving the fibre ready again. The new goal is to build and attach both muscles.
reaction: I didn't expect relaxation to require ATP too.
reason: The biceps sheaths have empty muscle-head spaces, so the relaxed fibre looks like a suitable piece to put into them.
expectation: The fibre should fill the biceps sheaths and help form a muscle with tendons.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs fibres; either muscle seems like a reasonable place to start.

effect: The fibre needed connective layers first; the automatic combination made bundles called fascicles, with enough for both muscles.
reaction: I hadn't realized the bundles needed to be prepared before fitting them into the sheaths.
reason: The fascicles are bundles of muscle fibres, and the biceps sheaths have empty spaces for them.
expectation: The fascicles should fill the biceps sheaths to form the muscle.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs bundles, so I could build it first.

effect: The fascicles filled the biceps sheaths, forming a biceps with tendons; the triceps still needs to be built.
reaction: The picture makes the connection from fibres through connective tissue to tendon clearer.
reason: There were enough fascicles for both muscles, and the triceps sheaths also have empty muscle-head spaces.
expectation: The fascicles should fill the triceps sheaths to form the triceps with tendons.

effect: The fascicles formed the triceps, so both muscles are ready to attach to the arm skeleton.
reaction: The three triceps heads converging on one tendon are clear in the picture.
reason: The biceps tendons lead toward the shoulder and radius, so I’ll attach it to the arm skeleton first.
expectation: The biceps should attach across the elbow, leaving the triceps to add.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the triceps first instead.

effect: The biceps is attached across the elbow, and the arm assembly still has an empty extensor slot.
reaction: The two poses make the biceps pulling to bend the elbow clearer.
reason: The triceps is the remaining muscle, and its tendon crosses the opposite side of the elbow, fitting the empty extensor slot.
expectation: The triceps should attach to the arm assembly and provide the opposing pull that straightens the elbow.

effect: The triceps filled the remaining slot and showed how its attachment straightens the elbow, completing both goals.
reaction: Seeing the two muscles pull from opposite sides made their different jobs clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the fibre shorten and then reset was worthwhile: it connected calcium and ATP to both pulling and relaxation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the two muscles was somewhat repetitive once the first sheath had been filled, though the pictures showed their different attachments.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the filaments slide past each other without shortening, and that resetting also uses ATP.

arbitrary.text: The need to add extracellular matrix before filling the muscle sheaths was not obvious to me beforehand, though the result explained the connective layers around the bundles.

continue.text: I would continue to see how these muscles work with other body systems; the connection between their attachments and opposite elbow movements was a useful hook.
